properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent, and no option is preferred.

WHERE IT CAME FROM: art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, item D15. The designer asked for "parallel composition in budgets: max as well as sum". The root cause (fact:root-cause-a-latency-budget-with-parallel-branches-is-judged-on-the-sum-while-its-worst-path-is-computed-beside-it-2026-09-29) found the max half ALREADY computed: budget_report's worst_path sums along DEPENDS_ON and takes the heaviest branch. But the verdict is always the plain sum. Measured: path 33 ms, sum 46 ms, a 40 ms limit, verdict `exceeded`.

SEARCHED ACCEPTED INTENT FIRST: cap:budget ("Sum contributions along the thread", verified) and the BL-11 "budgets that cannot lie" work. Neither rules on which rollup the verdict should read for a path-cumulative quantity.

═══ OPTIONS ═══

(a) DECLARED BY THE AUTHOR. A Constraint field, e.g. `composition: total | worst_path`. The verdict reads the declared rollup, and both are still reported. Absent means nobody said: keep today's verdict and SAY that the path was not used, the way unstated contributions are named, not zeroed.
⚠️ Counter: another field an author must know to set. The designer never read budget_report's description, and would it have found this one?

(b) INFERRED from quantity or unit (time means path, mass means total).
⚠️ Counter: the same unit composes both ways. CPU-milliseconds across a batch add up; latency along a request does not. An inference would silently change verdicts on designs that never asked. This project has refused inference-from-absence before (dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state, and Capability.delivery's rejected fix).

(c) GATE ON THE PATH WHENEVER ONE EXISTS.
⚠️ Counter: a mass budget whose parts happen to have DEPENDS_ON among them would suddenly gate on one chain and under-count. That is the dangerous direction for a maximum.

(d) INSTRUCTION ONLY. Keep the sum verdict, and have `constrains` say that DEPENDS_ON among contributors yields a path total.
⚠️ Counter: the measured false `exceeded` stays. It only becomes explainable.

(e) FINER CONTRIBUTORS, for overlap INSIDE one part. The designer's commit and rule delta are phases within one operation, and today a contribution is one number per node. Contributions per Flow step, or per sub-component, would let phases overlap.
⚠️ Counter: modelling every phase as a node multiplies nodes and edges, the very cost the same report complains of (items I4 and I24).
properties.name: OPEN — should a budget Constraint declare how its quantity composes: summed over every contributor (mass, cost, area) or along the worst path (latency, where parallel branches take the max)? The verdict would then read the declared rollup, not always the sum
